display.purpose: Hero h1 only. One per page at 700 weight, fluid clamp(2.8rem, 7.5vw, 5.2rem), -0.045em tracking.

section.purpose: Landing-page section h2 and callout headings (700 weight, fluid clamp(1.7rem, 3.5vw, 2.7rem), -0.035em).

body.purpose: Default prose, text-900 on background-50, capped at 70ch for legal copy and 42rem for marketing leads.

mono.purpose: Code, compact row metadata, comparison headers, and raw URLs — JetBrains Mono.

motion.name: entrance

motion.name: interaction

narrative.overview: A dark, teal-tinted editorial register aligned with Fathom. Near-black teal surfaces, a soft radial mint glow, large tight-set Inter, and a single mint accent give the site a quiet, bookish confidence. Cards use a restrained gradient and a hairline border rather than shadows; buttons are pills; the shell is 1080px wide. It remains technical enough for the AT Protocol audience without becoming a protocol explainer.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-only: #0B1416 page, #121F24 raised surface, no light scheme or light-dark() tokens
High contrast: text-900 on background-50, text-950 headings, text-700 muted copy
Large editorial type: 5.2rem hero, 2.7rem section headings, tight tracking
One mint accent (#2DD4BF) for links, focus, eyebrows, active nav, the wordmark dot and primary actions
Tonal + border surfaces: 20px cards with a subtle vertical gradient, no shadows or glass
Pill buttons and a 1080px shell, matching Fathom's proportions
Sans navigation and footer; JetBrains Mono reserved for code and compact metadata
Calm motion: exponential-eased entrances, decisive press feedback, reduced-motion collapse

rules.name: The Dark-Only Rule
rules.body: The site has one colour scheme. Do not add a prefers-color-scheme branch, theme toggle or light-dark() token. A light version would be a separate visual system.

rules.name: The High-Contrast Rule
rules.body: Body text is text-900 on background-50; headings are text-950. Muted copy is text-700 and must clear 4.5:1 against its surface. Never use text-500 or darker for body copy.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Mint is the interactive signal: links, focus rings, list markers, active nav, eyebrow labels, the wordmark dot and primary buttons. Primary buttons use a dark teal #042F2E label, never white.

rules.name: The Tonal + Border Rule
rules.body: Cards, lists and callouts step away from the page through a subtle gradient plus a 1px border. There are no drop shadows, no glass and no decorative blur.

rules.name: The Typography-First Rule
rules.body: Visual hierarchy is established through weight, size and tracking — never through colour splashes. If a heading needs an accent colour to feel important, the weight or size is wrong.

rules.name: The One Display Rule
rules.body: The hero h1 is the only element at Display size (700) on any page. Section headings step down to Section Title (700, 2.7rem maximum).

rules.name: The No-Glass, No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow, no backdrop-filter, no glassmorphism. The only gradient is the surface treatment on cards/callouts and the radial page glow.

rules.name: The Feedback-Not-Decoration Rule
rules.body: Animation plays on content entrance and on direct manipulation only — never as ambient looping decoration. Entrances use ease-out-expo; interaction uses ease-out-quart.

dos: Do keep body text text-900 on background-50 and headings text-950 — contrast is the system's signature
Do treat the site as dark-only; update tokens rather than adding a light variant
Do use mint (primary-500) for interactive signals and primary actions
Do differentiate surfaces with a subtle gradient + 1px border, never a shadow
Do use text-wrap: balance on headings and text-wrap: pretty on prose
Do cap body text lines at 60–70ch for legal copy and 42rem for marketing leads
Do test every colour against its background for ≥4.5:1 contrast (body) and ≥3:1 (large text)
Do provide a prefers-reduced-motion fallback for every animation
Do use sans for nav, footer and eyebrows; reserve JetBrains Mono for code and compact metadata
Do trust the reader — the AT Protocol audience is technically literate; state the value clearly without over-explaining
donts: Don't add a light theme, prefers-color-scheme branch or theme toggle
Don't use drop shadows, backdrop-filter or glassmorphism
Don't use the SaaS startup template kit: no gradient hero backgrounds, no animated counters, no glassmorphism
Don't make a primary button an inverse white/dark pair — primary actions are mint with dark teal labels
Don't set body copy lighter than text-700 against the page background
Don't nest cards inside cards — if a container needs a sub-container, reconsider the layout
Don't animate CSS layout properties — use transform and opacity only
Don't over-explain the AT Protocol to the audience — link to atproto.com for background; the site sells the app, not the protocol
